text:
In a season Detroit's captain has spent away from the team, the Red Wings have hung a banner of Emmitt Finnie outside Little Caesars Arena where Dylan Larkin's used to be, as Sean Shapiro of EP Rinkside noted on Nov. 19. That's quite a sign of the times for a 21-year-old taken 201st overall in 2023.

He's earning the billing. Finnie plays almost 19 minutes a night, and his ice time has climbed two more over the last ten games. At five on five Detroit gets about 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, more than eleven points better than without him, the biggest gap on the team. He has elite wheels too: his bursts over 20 mph sit in the top 1% of the league.

The points have stalled. He's gone seven games without one, on about four expected goals' worth of chances, while the Wings lost six of them. Our numbers read it as a dry spell, not a decline: his 7 goals in 22 games match his chances almost exactly. Watch whether the finishing returns before the losing defines Detroit's November.
